rationale: The claim describes the paper's Figure 2 as a two-panel time series in which a hypothetical unemployment rate driven only by job-finding fluctuations (x-bar/(x-bar+f_t), top panel) tracks the actual unemployment rate at every cyclical increase, and a hypothetical rate driven only by exit fluctuations (x_t/(x_t+f-bar), bottom panel) tracks unemployment through ~1985 then flattens cyclically aside from a 2008 spike. The run did produce figure2.pdf files (output/two_state/figure2.pdf and output/two_state_1948_2010/figure2.pdf; the exact expected path output/figure2.pdf does not exist), but the plotting code (run_two_state.py:196, 'Figure 2: F and X against the unemployment rate') emits a two-panel SCATTER of the raw job-finding probability F vs. the unemployment rate (left) and the exit probability X vs. the unemployment rate (right). Confirmed by reading both PDFs: x-axis is 'unemployment rate' (0.03-0.11), y-axes are F (~0.32-0.65) and X (~0.025-0.048), no time dimension. This is a different figure from the paper's Figure 2: it has no time axis, does not construct or plot the hypothetical unemployment-rate series (x-bar/(x-bar+f_t) or x_t/(x_t+f-bar) — those hypotheticals are only built inside table1_decomp.py for the regression decomposition, not plotted here), and therefore cannot exhibit or be checked against the claim's core temporal features (tracking at every increase; 1985 flattening; 2008 spike). The scatter does not contradict the underlying economics (F falls, X rises with unemployment), but essentially none of the described structural features of Figure 2 are present, so the claim cannot be verified from the produced figure. fix_severity.json records only one major data-handling fix (tail-splice), unrelated to the figure's structure.
